# Base model selection matrix (slice s9)

<!-- Generated by `python -m research.base_model.render` from selection_matrix.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

> Research prototype, not for clinical use. This matrix is evidence for choosing a base model to fine-tune; it makes no clinical claim.

Owner: ธนาพล. Sources retrieved on 2026-09-26. Every cell cites a primary source (official model card, license text, technical report, or official GitHub). `null` means the source was checked and the value is not reported there.

**Status: `pending_preliminary_experiments`. Final selection: `null`.** No winner is declared. The choice follows the preliminary experiments (proposal 2.3), scored with the rubric below.

## Candidates

- **MedGemma 27B multimodal (google/medgemma-27b-it)**: The multimodal instruction-tuned variant. Not google/medgemma-27b-text-it (text-only), which cannot take images.
- **Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B)**: The post-trained vision-language release (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration). A general model, not medically trained.
- **Lingshu-32B (lingshu-medical-mllm/Lingshu-32B)**: Medical MLLM built on Qwen2.5-VL-32B. True size about 33.45B parameters, larger than 'approximately 27B'.

### Within-group rankings

None. No comparable group contains the same benchmark, metric and setting for two or more candidates, so no cross-candidate ranking is possible from reported numbers. Candidates are compared in the preliminary experiments.

## Pre-declared selection rubric

Declared on 2026-09-26, before any preliminary fine-tune result exists (no file under `research/results/`).

Selection data: Preliminary fine-tune results on the project's own validation split only (patient-level split, proposal 3.4). Official test sets are never used to choose the base model.

Hard constraints (a candidate failing any one is excluded):

- Open weights downloadable for local fine-tuning (no API-only access).
- License permits fine-tuning, and either permits the intended open-weight release of the derivative or a human decision accepting the release terms is recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md.
- Runs entirely on team-controlled machines for MIMIC data (PhysioNet rule, proposal 1.3.4).
- Stage-3 LoRA fits 8x B200 per the estimate AND per the Tier-2 measured peak memory.
- True parameter count is reported; a model is never relabelled to a different scale.

| Criterion | Weight | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| prelim_task_quality | 0.30 | Validation-split quality after the Tier-2/3 preliminary fine-tune (CXR findings macro-F1, CT report quality, department suggestion accuracy), same budget per candidate |
| license_release_fit | 0.20 | Compatibility of the license with an open-weight release of the derivative (permissive > conditional > incompatible) |
| measured_memory_throughput | 0.15 | Tier-2 measured peak memory headroom and tokens/s on one B200 |
| base_zero_shot_quality | 0.10 | Base model zero-shot quality on the validation split before fine-tuning (proposal Table 3.2 comparator) |
| scale_fidelity | 0.10 | Closeness of the true parameter count to approximately 27B |
| ecosystem_support | 0.10 | transformers / peft / DeepSpeed / vLLM support without custom patches |
| contamination_risk | 0.05 | Lower known or unknown overlap with evaluation sources scores higher |
| **total** | **1.00** | |

Tie-breaks, in order: (1) More permissive license. (2) Lower measured peak memory per GPU. (3) Smaller true parameter count.

Fairness: Every candidate gets the same data, token budget, LoRA rank grid, optimizer search budget and evaluation. Any exception is disclosed in the results.

## Decisions needed (humans)

- **medgemma-release-terms** (medgemma-27b-it): HAI-DEF section 3.1/3.2 require the use restrictions to flow down to any distributed derivative, plus notices, a copy of the terms and (when applicable) Health Regulatory Authorization. Does this allow the project's intended open-weight release? Must be settled before MedGemma can be the final base.
- **lingshu-true-scale** (lingshu-32b): Lingshu-32B has 33,452,718,336 parameters. Does it count as 'approximately 27B' for the headline claim, or must any result be reported at its true scale?
- **lingshu-upstream-license** (lingshu-32b): Lingshu is MIT-licensed but built on Qwen2.5-VL (Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct is tagged apache-2.0). Confirm which notice obligations carry into a release of our derivative.
- **mimic-cxr-overlap** (medgemma-27b-it, lingshu-32b): Both medical candidates were trained on MIMIC-CXR. Every base-vs-fine-tuned MIMIC-CXR comparison (proposal Table 3.2) must disclose this. Should MIMIC-CXR results for these bases be reported as contaminated?
